Main.sentence: LGBTQ people are individuals who are ___E:lesbian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesbian)___ , ___E:gay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_men)___ , ___E:bisexual U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexual)___ , ___E:transgender U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender)___ , or ___E:queer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer)___ .

Many variants [a] of the initialism are used, such as those incorporating ___E:questioning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Questioning_(sexuality_and_gender))___ , ___E:intersex U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intersex)___ , ___E:asexual U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asexuality)___ , ___E:aromantic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aromanticism)___ , ___E:agender U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agender)___ , and other individuals.
The group is generally conceived as broadly encompassing all individuals who are part of a ___E:sexual or gender minority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_and_gender_minorities)___ .
LGBTQ people express a broad array of sexual and gender minority identities.
The alternative umbrella gender, sexual, and romantic minorities is sometimes used for this group.

Common variations of the initialism include LGBT , LGBT+ , LGBTQ+ , and LGBTQIA+ .

LGBTQ people may participate in the LGBTQ community, which may be defined by shared ___E:LGBTQ culture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_culture)___ , by shared geography (such as ___E:gay villages U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_village)___ ), or by participation in LGBTQ-focused organizations.

The LGBTQ community includes elements such as ___E:LGBTQ social movements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_social_movements)___ (including ___E:LGBTQ rights organizations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_rights_organization)___ ), ___E:LGBTQ student groups in schools and universities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay%E2%80%93straight_alliance)___ , and ___E:LGBTQ-affirming religious groups U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ-affirming_religious_groups)___ .

LGBTQ activists and sociologists see LGBTQ community-building as a counterweight to ___E:heterosexism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterosexism)___ , ___E:homophobia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homophobia)___ , ___E:biphobia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biphobia)___ , ___E:transphobia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transphobia)___ , ___E:sexualism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexualism)___ , and other ___E:conformist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conformist)___ pressures that exist in the larger society.
Not all LGBTQ people consider themselves part of the LGBTQ community. [citation needed]
LGBTQ culture varies widely by geography and the identity of the participants.

Not all LGBTQ people identify with LGBTQ culture; this may be due to geographic distance, unawareness of the subculture's existence, fear of ___E:social stigma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_stigma)___ or a preference for remaining unidentified with sexuality- or gender-based subcultures or communities.

The ___E:Queercore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queercore)___ and ___E:Gay Shame U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_Shame)___ movements critique what they see as the commercialization and self-imposed "ghettoization" of LGBTQ culture.
The history of LGBTQ people dates back to the first recorded instances of same-sex love and diverse gender identities and sexualities in cultures around the world.

In many cultures this history has involved marginalization and persecution, such that these histories have only in recent decades been pursued and interwoven into more mainstream historical narratives.
In 1994, the annual observance of ___E:LGBT History Month U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_History_Month)___ began in the United States, and it has since been picked up in other countries.

This observance involves highlighting the history of the people, ___E:LGBTQ rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_rights)___ and related ___E:civil rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights)___ movements.

It is observed during October in the United States, to include ___E:National Coming Out Day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Coming_Out_Day)___ on October 11.  In the United Kingdom it has been observed during February since 2005: ___E:Section 28 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Section_28)___ , which had prohibited local authorities from "promoting" homosexuality was repealed in England and Wales in 2003, while the same legislation (named Section 2a in the Scottish legislation) was repealed by the ___E:Scottish parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_parliament)___ in 2000.   A celebrated achievement in LGBTQ history occurred when ___E:Queen Beatrix U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Beatrix)___ signed a law making Netherlands the ___E:first country to legalize same-sex marriage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_the_Netherlands)___ in 2001,  and another when Ireland became ___E:the first country to legalise same-sex marriage by popular vote in 2015 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirty-fourth_Amendment_of_the_Constitution_of_Ireland)___ .

The legal rights held by LGBTQ people vary greatly by country or jurisdiction—ranging from the legal recognition of ___E:same-sex marriage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage)___ to the ___E:death penalty for homosexuality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_punishment_for_homosexuality)___ .
An example of such protections are legal prohibitions against ___E:incitement to hatred and violence against LGBTQ people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-LGBTQ_rhetoric)___ .

Even in jurisdictions with strong protections for LGBTQ rights, they may still be subject to ___E:discrimination against LGBTQ people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination_against_LGBTQ_people)___ .

Discrimination against LGBTQ people can manifest in legal, institutional, and social forms.  : 1 This includes ___E:discrimination directed specifically at lesbians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination_against_lesbians)___ , ___E:at homosexuals more broadly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination_against_homosexuals)___ , ___E:at gay men U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination_against_gay_men)___ , ___E:at bisexuals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination_against_bisexuals)___ , ___E:at transgender people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination_against_transgender_people)___ , ___E:at asexual people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination_against_asexual_people)___ , ___E:at intersex people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination_against_intersex_people)___ , and ___E:at non-binary people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrimination_against_non-binary_people)___ .
___E:Opposition to LGBTQ rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opposition_to_LGBTQ_rights)___ exists worldwide.

While laws are "a necessary foundation to achieve equality ... protections under the law are not sufficient to eliminate prejudice", and "social equality is not synonymous with equality under the law", according to ___E:Ilan Meyer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilan_Meyer)___ .

According to a study by the ___E:European Parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament)___ 's internal policy body in 2012: "To resolve the vast majority of problems faced by LGBTI people, individuals, society, organisations and authorities must stop regarding their differences as factors which require differential treatment.

While this seems self evident, such shifts in attitude cannot be achieved through one-off, short term action, nor through legislation alone. ... in some areas a change of views of some groups may simply not be possible."
Some countries practice ___E:censorship of LGBTQ issues U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Censorship_of_LGBTQ_issues)___ .
Social divides exist over the social acceptance of LGBTQ people, including ___E:societal attitudes toward homosexuality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Societal_attitudes_toward_homosexuality)___ .
LGBTQ movements are ___E:social movements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_movements)___ that advocate for the inclusion, recognition, and rights of LGBTQ people.
These movements work to secure legal rights, or enact broader social changes aimed at advancing equality and inclusion.
In addition, LGBTQ movements and communities work to advance ___E:LGBTQ culture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_culture)___ .

LGBTQ people may face disparities in access to care, targeted public health interventions, and the impact of stigma on physical and mental well-being.  : 2 The ___E:psychology of LGBTQ people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_psychology)___ covers aspects such as identity development including the ___E:coming out U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_out)___ process, parenting and family practices and support for LGBTQ individuals.
